title: SFI protests against Keralam Higher Education Minister
content: SFI activists raise slogans against Roji M. John in protest against the alleged failure by the government to take action over the ‘police excesses’ on students at the university hostel

title: Some oligarchs blocking entry of Starlink in India: Elon Musk
content: Elon Musk has claimed that certain oligarchs are obstructing Starlink's entry into the Indian market. Starlink has already established the necessary infrastructure and is prepared to launch its services. The company aims to provide affordable broadband connectivity to areas lacking internet access. Regulatory approvals are awaited before the commercial rollout can commence in India. Collaboration with local telecom operators has been a key element in Starlink's strategy for success.

title: IIT-B puts on hold 2026 rules on tough penalties for cheating
content: IIT-Bombay’s senate has halted new penalties for academic misconduct, reverting to the 2015 policy for upcoming examinations. This decision follows the recent death of a student suspected of cheating during an exam. An interim procedure allows faculty to document suspected dishonesty while encouraging student accounts on a separate form. Faculty members and students will present their cases before a disciplinary committee after the examination period.

title: 'We'll do it': PM Modi gives slogan for 2047 goals
content: PM Narendra Modi delivered a speech highlighting his 25 years in government and the goal of developed India by 2047. He called upon citizens to commit to this ambitious target and emphasized the power of the people. Modi reiterated the importance of extraordinary goals, linking good governance to societal inclusion. He reflected on his journey from humble beginnings to leadership in the BJP.

title: 'Fight goes on’: 87-yr-old woman dies after becoming symbol of Spain housing crisis
content: María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, died in a hospital after being evicted from her home. Her eviction triggered nationwide protests highlighting the housing crisis afflicting Spain. Activists voiced anger over Maricarmen's death as a symbol of the struggle against rising rents and evictions. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez offered condolences, acknowledging the impact of her case on public sentiment.

title: Loans set to get dearer as RBI hikes repo rate after 44 months
content: The Reserve Bank of India has announced a 25 basis points increase in the repo rate to 5.5%. This decision reflects growing inflation pressures and stronger than anticipated economic growth. The rise in interest rates will lead to higher loan EMIs, impacting consumption during the festive season. Banks are expected to increase fixed deposit rates following this policy change.

title: Google ordered to halt data center work in 'Texas of Europe; company admits ‘concerns’
content: Google has received an order to halt construction on its data center projects in Muhos and Kajaani. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Agency has mandated that construction continues only after environmental impact assessments. Google acknowledged the concerns raised and stated that it would comply with the authority's guidance. The company has emphasized its commitment to biodiversity plans, including extensive tree planting.

title: Anti-CEC protests: Oppn, police face off again; Rahul says won’t stop till Gyanesh quits
content: Opposition members from the INDIA bloc attempted to stage a protest demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. They were detained by Delhi Police less than a kilometer from their protest site at Jantar Mantar. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge organized the lunch gathering, where the protest plan was discussed. Difficulties in moving their buses led to further confrontations with police as they sought to demonstrate.

title: US-based woman files case against parents for property share; Karnataka HC rejects it
content: The case involves a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act. The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property.

title: Living Planet Report: WWF finds 73% global wildlife decline; India shows recovery gains
content: A global decline of 73% in monitored wildlife populations occurred between 1970 and 2022. India has successfully improved populations of tigers, one-horned rhinos, and Ganga river dolphins. The report highlights threats like habitat loss, climate change, and pollution affecting wildlife. Despite the negative trends, about half of monitored populations are stable or increasing globally. Targeted conservation efforts in India demonstrate the potential for wildlife recovery and biodiversity preservation.

title: Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission
content: National Medical Commission has issued guidelines restricting the use of AI in medical advertising and patient testimonials. Registered medical practitioners and hospitals must not engage in creating synthetic content or manipulating search rankings. Claims of being the best or offering guaranteed results are also prohibited under these rules. Additionally, offering discounts or referrals that encourage unnecessary consultations is not allowed.

title: Hollywood actor buys 25 acres of damaged Hawaiian land to restore rainforest
content: Hollywood actor Jason Scott Lee transformed 25 acres of damaged Hawaiian land into a simple, self-sufficient home. The property was once littered with car parts, paint cans and debris. Lee grew taro, raised chickens and embraced natural farming while working to restore the rainforest, reflecting his decision to pursue a simpler life away from Hollywood.

title: 11,000 wētāpunga released over 15 years now thriving on two islands
content: Wētāpunga, the largest giant wētā species in New Zealand, is rebounding after years of decline caused by habitat destruction and invasive predators. Thanks to dedicated conservation efforts, more than 11,000 wētāpunga have been bred and released into protected areas. With at least four generations now thriving in the wild, the program aims to sustain their growing populations and ensure their future survival.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school; 10 years later, Board votes to close it
content: Priscilla Chan's tuition-free private school in California has shut down after receiving over $125 million in funding. The school, which aimed to support low-income children and families, faced challenges leading to its closure. About 540 children were enrolled, and families expressed concern over the abrupt announcement of the closure. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative pledged $50 million to assist with transition services and education savings accounts.

title: Bihar teen hits Candy Crush Level 22,222, enters record book
content: Shubham Kumar, a 19-year-old student from Government Engineering College, Siwan, recently reached Level 22,222 in Candy Crush Saga. His achievement has been recognized by the International Book of Records as the highest level reached by a teenager. After setting the record, he reported reaching further levels in the King Community, demonstrating ongoing dedication to the game. The Bihar government department has congratulated Kumar on his remarkable accomplishment.

title: Make a good film, repay your debts: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav
content: Supreme Court has maintained the condition for Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore for his appeal. Yadav took a loan of Rs 5 crore in 2010 for a film that never completed, which has accrued interest. His counsel mentioned he secured Rs 1.15 crore and aims to sell property to cover remaining dues. The court suggested producing a successful film may help him repay the debts.

title: Assam CM Himanta Sarma says woman sent to Bangladesh safe, son counters CM
content: Mumtaz Begum, a woman expelled to Bangladesh, remains untraceable by her family despite official claims of her safety. Her son, Momruz Ali, is pleading for government assistance to locate her in either country. The Gauhati High Court directed authorities to find Mumtaz and provide interim compensation to her husband. Reports indicate that searches in Bangladesh yielded no results for her whereabouts so far.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $1.6m philanthropy: How are they helping 20,000 kids?
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have made children a major focus of their charitable work through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Their efforts include a $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs commitment, a $1 million inclusive Kansas City playground, literacy programs reaching more than 20,000 students, community grants and food support for families facing hardship.

title: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation: Why are Ed and Donna Kelce involved?
content: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation has not posted since January 2026. They continue their charitable work through Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab. Donna Kelce met with Ignition Lab students during a Kansas City Chiefs game. Ed Kelce visited first graders at Operation Breakthrough. Travis Kelce’s foundation got its first post after January on Travis’ birthday.

title: Mamata Banerjee’s Delhi arrival fuels buzz over INDIA bloc meet with President
content: TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee's arrival in Delhi has heightened anticipation for the requested meeting with President Droupadi Murmu. The opposition bloc is awaiting confirmation for a meeting date between October 7 and 9. The delegation has been limited to ten members as requested by the President's Secretariat. CPI(M)'s John Brittas has submitted a petition for constitutional intervention regarding the Election Commission.

title: With PM Modi set to visit Ottawa, India & Canada back CEPA
content: India and Canada are currently engaged in the fifth round of talks for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Both countries aim to sign the CEPA during Prime Minister Modi's anticipated visit to Canada. The visit is tentatively scheduled for December 11-13, just before the G20 summit in Florida. Leaders from both nations envision boosting bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030.

title: Centre cites Supreme Court order, seeks to void Jharkhand DGP appointment
content: Supreme Court has agreed to hear the application from the Centre regarding Tadasha Mishra's appointment as Jharkhand DGP. The appointment has been challenged due to its conflict with procedures set in the SC's 2006 Prakash Singh judgement. Moreover, the Centre claimed that prior DGP appointments in Jharkhand were also illegal for similar reasons. Mishra's appointment occurred shortly before her retirement, which raised legal concerns.

title: Medical trips costliest in both rural & urban areas
content: Health and medical trips incurred the highest expenses in rural and urban areas during a one-year period. The average expenditure for these trips was notably higher in urban than rural areas. Pilgrimage travel accounted for the largest share of trips taken throughout the year. Accommodation and transport were significant expenditures for health and medical trips, underscoring their financial impact.

title: 'Cash-for transfers' WA chats part of CBI dossier on Mann OSD
content: A set of WhatsApp chats has emerged, alleging monetary transactions involving senior Punjab government officials and DSPs. CBI's dossier includes these chats as they prepare to interrogate CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman. Allegations suggest that intermediaries received bribes for influencing transfers and policy formulations affecting IAS and IPS officers. Additionally, documents indicate potential irregularities in real estate projects and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority.

title: Oceans connect, not divide nations, PM Modi says, calls for secure maritime order
content: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of maritime connectivity and proposed a ceasefire plan for the Black Sea. His vision promotes cooperation and mutual benefit among nations to ensure maritime security. Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan highlighted the interconnectedness of national security and economic security. He urged for collective action among regions to tackle maritime threats effectively.

title: 'One student, one day': CUET-UG 2027 may get shorter, simpler
content: CUET-UG 2027 may implement notable changes to streamline the examination experience for students. Candidates could see a reduction in the number of subjects from five to four over time. The proposed changes also include shortening the duration of individual papers to enhance efficiency. Subject grouping may allow related papers to be scheduled together for a single-day examination.

title: FBI foils alleged ISIS-linked attack plot at Mall of America by 18-year-old
content: Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, an 18-year-old, was arrested for planning an attack on the Mall of America. He agreed to buy an AK-47 and ammunition from an undercover FBI agent posing as an ISIS member. Mohamud expressed intentions to kill non-Muslims during a scheduled Hmong arts celebration. US authorities stated that his radicalization was identified well before his plan could be executed.

title: UK's oldest Indian restaurant owner accuses Crown Estate of not valuing curry traditions
content: Ranjit Mathrani, the owner of Veeraswamy, is taking legal action against the Crown Estate over lease refusal. He believes this reflects an undervaluation of Indian culinary traditions compared to European cuisine. The restaurant has a significant historical background with notable patrons, including Indian leaders. The Crown Estate maintains its decision is based on structural issues and not culinary bias.

title: ​IndiGo flight hit by lightning, damage found only after landing in Lucknow
content: An IndiGo flight experienced a lightning strike while approaching Lucknow, damaging its nose radome. The aircraft landed safely, with all 110 people onboard unharmed. The severity of the damage became clear only after the flight was parked. Authorities confirmed that the aircraft will undergo a comprehensive inspection and necessary repairs before service. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has been notified as per standard procedure.

title: A lunch, then a march: How Rahul-led opposition once again kept police guessing
content: The episode was the latest example of a 'dhappa' style protest that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have recently used. The latest episode began after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge announced an INDIA bloc sit-in at Jantar Mantar following the lunch. "Today, we will hold a sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar. Until our demands are met, we will continue to stage such protests," Kharge announced.

title: NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist Shabir Shah in 1996 funeral violence case
content: A Jammu NIA court rejected the bail application of Shabir Ahmad Shah, linked to a 30-year-old mob violence case. This case relates to violence during a terrorist's funeral procession in Srinagar, which Shah allegedly incited. The court expressed concern about potential threats to national security and the safety of protected witnesses. Shah argued that the investigation was reopened without justification and emphasized delays in legal actions.

title: Grenade seizure case: Pakistan-based ultra declared ‘proclaimed offender’
content: A special NIA court in Jammu has declared Nazir Hussain a proclaimed offender regarding grenade seizures. Hussain, originally from Hari village, is believed to be hiding in Pakistan currently. The court noted that previous non-bailable arrest warrants could not be executed due to his absence from home. Additionally, multiple attempts to compel Hussain to surrender have been unsuccessful.

title: India’s first high-altitude snow leopard safari flagged off in Ladakh
content: Ladakh has commenced India's first high-altitude wildlife safari that highlights snow leopard trails and community involvement. Vinai Kumar Saxena, the lieutenant governor, emphasized the importance of coexisting wildlife and development. The Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation Society is coordinating this project with local forest departments. The mapped safari routes traverse significant wildlife areas, including Hemis National Park and Changthang.

title: ‘Nobody can stop Bumrah & Bhuvi’: Ashwin’s bold prediction as pacer makes India return
content: Ravichandran Ashwin asserts that Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s display in New Zealand might have a significant impact on his chances for World Cup selection. Having last participated in an ODI in 2022, Bhuvneshwar is set to make his return to international cricket. His capacity to swing the ball could enhance India's bowling lineup for next year’s championship.

title: Delhi building collapse: Pregnant woman, child among 3 killed in Seemapuri; 8 injured
content: In Seemapuri, Delhi, a tragic building collapse resulted in the loss of three lives, including a child, with eight others injured. The incident, which occurred around 3.15 PM, activated swift rescue operations by both locals and authorities. Concerns about the building’s structural stability arose following recent earthquakes in Uttarakhand. Investigations into the cause of the collapse are ongoing, with local traffic also disrupted due to the incident.

title: From 'vote chori' to 'chita andolan': Street protests return with a new playbook
content: From 'vote chori' protests and women’s safety marches to 'Chita Andolan', the streets are getting politically crowded again. But the old politics of protest now comes with a new playbook. Younger voices, looser networks, social media, viral slogans and issue-based mobilisation are changing how protests begin, spread and draw attention.

title: Out on bail after rape allegation, Porel named in Bengal squad for Ranji opener
content: Wicketkeeper-batter Abhishek Porel has been included in Bengal's squad for their upcoming Ranji Trophy match. He was previously arrested on allegations of rape but has since been granted bail. The team has named a strong squad with senior pacers Mohammed Shami and Akash Deep included. Bengal's match against Delhi is set to take place in Kalyani to mark the season opener.

title: ‘Changed Shreyas’ grip & backlift’: How Nayar helped India T20I captain bounce back
content: Facing a troubling drop in performance, with no scores exceeding 30 in his last ten T20I outings, Shreyas Iyer turned to Abhishek Nayar for help. Their two-hour conversation revolved around critical adjustments to Iyer's batting style. The results were evident as Iyer responded with a stellar 102 not out in the first T20I against West Indies, underscoring his tenacity and capacity to rebound from tough situations.

title: White House Denies Trump Suggested Iran Should "Take Out" US Cities
content: Democrats -- who control the state of California where both Los Angeles and San Diego are located -- accused the 80-year-old Republican president of encouraging Iran to hit the two urban centers.

title: FBI Arrests ISIS Sympathiser For Plotting Mass Shooting At Mall Of America
content: In July, Mohamud allegedly said he wanted to kill 30 to 60 people at the Mall of America because he claimed its owners were Jewish, and he wanted to kill non-Muslims.

title: Satya Nadella, Elon Musk Among Top Tech CEOs To Receive US Science Medal
content: Computer mogul Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will get the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the top award in its field.

title: Trump Says He Should Win Nobel Peace Prize, But Has Doubts About Winning
content: Since his return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world's most prestigious award.

title: Trump Says US Has "Taken Away" Iran's Nuclear Power
content: US President Donald Trump said the war with Iran will end "very quickly" and claimed that oil prices will "come tumbling down", while asserting that the US has taken away Iran's nuclear power.

title: Children Among 28 Killed In Ukraine As Russia Intensifies Attacks
content: President Volodymyr Zelensky said three of the dead were just 12 months old while another was aged eight. Another child's body was pulled from the rubble in the evening, the interior ministry said.

title: BRS Accuses Telangana MLA Of "Inappropriately Touching" Girl On Bus
content: In a video that has gone viral, Ranga Reddy (70), MLA from Ibrahimpatnam, is seen having a conversation with two girl students on the Congress government's 'Mahalakshmi' free bus scheme for women.

title: Taslima Nasrin In Kolkata, Says Will Stay For Durga Puja Next Year
content: "I will certainly be here next year. I absolutely love the Puja celebrations here; it feels like a grand art exhibition," Taslima Nasrin said.

title: Saudi Says 3 Killed In Houthi Attacks On Its Airports As Conflict Deepens
content: The Iran-backed fighters earlier took responsibility for a flurry of attacks that included firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport as the conflict deepens with Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government.

title: Assam Paramilitary Force Personnel Dies Of Dengue In Gujarat
content: The death - first among visiting security forces - underscores the vector-borne outbreak in the capital city of Gujarat.

title: Centre Challenges Appointment Of Jharkhand Police Chief In Supreme Court
content: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta mentioned the application before a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which agreed to hear and list the Centre's application.

title: 'SIR' In America Too? India Cue In Trump's Mass Citizenship Check For Voters
content: Having got the nod from the US Supreme Court, Donald Trump's push for a voter roll "cleanup" puts citizenship at its centre. Arguments for India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) have also centred on "illegal immigrants". Data remains scarce. Let's map the similarities and the nuance.

title: INDIA Bloc Protest Highlights: Bus Carrying Detained Rahul Gandhi Punctured By Congress Workers
content: On Tuesday, Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and other Congress MPs, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises, barely 200 metres from the poll body office, and asked to be allowed to meet the Election Commissioners.

title: Syria Says Country's Northeast Oil Pipeline Damaged In "Sabotage Attack"
content: Years of civil war before the fall of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in late 2024 devastated Syria's oil, gas and electricity sectors, with the country becoming heavily reliant on imports to meet its needs.

title: 4 Students Killed After Entering Water Tank In Mathura School
content: The incident took place on Tuesday night at Maharishi Parini Sanskrit Vidhyalaya, also known as Vrindavan Gurukulam, in Chaitanya Vihar Colony under Vrindavan police station.

title: Captain Smit Machchhar's Health Is Improving: Foreign Ministry
content: Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani citizen, with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for use in emergencies, seriously injuring him.

title: Undercover FBI Employee Sold Teen Rifle For $600, Then Arrested Him
content: The 18-year-old had been under investigation for nearly two years, trading messages with a confidential informant, before agents sold him the rifle and ammunition and arrested him on the spot, they said.
